title: Good-Faith Months for Recent Repayments — Benefit Overpayment Accounts Desk Guidance
content:
A recent voluntary repayment earns good-faith months on a new Benefit Overpayment Accounts repayment plan, added to the plan months. The gap is measured in calendar days from the most recent repayment received on the overpayment to the handling date; the most recent repayment received is the repayment entry with the latest booking date on the overpayment's ledger.

| Calendar days from the most recent repayment to the handling date | Good-faith months added |
|---|---|
| 90 or fewer (the recent-payment days) | 3, the recent good-faith extension |
| More than 90, up to 180 (the older-payment days) | 1, the older good-faith extension |
| More than 180, or no repayment at all | None |

## Points the desk applies

- Exactly 90 days earns 3 months; 91 days earns 1 month.
- Exactly 180 days earns 1 month; 181 days earns none.
- Only repayments on the overpayment the plan is set on are looked at.

## Hypothetical cases

| Most recent repayment received | Handling date | Days | Months added |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 30 May | 90 | 3 |
| 1 March | 31 May | 91 | 1 |
| 1 March | 28 August | 180 | 1 |
| None on the ledger | Any | — | None |
